analysis:
The only change is a documentation addition in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1370-1382). It describes the Qwen inline MTP assistant: it speculates for a single decode row only, other rows run ordinary decode that may chain, and target hidden rows are appended to the assistant history at finalize. It also names rollback env switches (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY) and a per-drafter opt-in (supportsOrdinaryDecodeHistory). The patch contains no executable code, and the doc does not alter any trust boundary, endpoint, key custody or attestation control.

I checked the described behavior against the threat model. The hidden-state history is held in process memory (TB-007, T-014, T-028), which is the same exposure class as existing KV and assistant state. The text claims no new persistence, no new disk artifact and no new wire field. It does not touch the SSD prefix-cache surface (T-041): no cache identity, HMAC naming, TTL or scope change, and the next paragraph on checkpoint coding is unchanged. The new env vars are rollback controls and not security gates. They are performance-affecting DARKBLOOM_* settings, so the existing DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification rejection of unrecognized performance-affecting settings should apply. That interaction depends on code outside the supplied evidence.

Remaining integration question: the actual implementation in EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift is not supplied. I could not verify cross-request isolation of the chained history (assistant history must not leak across rows or tenants when membership changes), or that the carry is cleared on request finish. This is a code-level question for whoever reviews that implementation, not a defect shown by this doc-only change.
